Milestone 1 — EDA & Volatility Regime Audit¶

UBS SIX-Listed Equities: UBSG, NESN, NOVN, ROP (Roche) vs. SMI¶

Project: Swiss Market Forecasting — Volatility Framework for IB Desk / Risk Management Author: Camilo Seydoux Data vintage: yfinance pull, 2026-07-24 (see data/raw/ for source CSVs and audit trail) Revision: v2 — addresses reviewer comments (regime-conditioned correlation, FX-beta pre/post CS-merger split, explicit NESN event-day call, embedded images)

Objective¶

Deliver the Milestone 1 deliverables scoped by Risk/IB desk stakeholders:

  • Price/return time series, 2005-present, for UBSG, NESN, NOVN, ROP(Roche) + SMI
  • Rolling volatility (21d, 63d) and regime identification (2008 GFC, 2015 CHF unpeg, 2020 COVID, 2022 rate-hiking cycle)
  • Correlation matrix (returns and volatility) across the four names, including whether that structure actually shifts during stress, tested directly rather than assumed
  • Stationarity tests (ADF/KPSS) on returns
  • FX-beta appendix: how much of observed co-movement is a common CHF/USD/EUR factor vs. genuine equity correlation, including a pre/post Credit Suisse-merger split for UBSG
  • Missing data / corporate action audit (documented separately, summarized here)

What this notebook does NOT do¶

This is explicitly EDA, not modeling. GJR-GARCH, Monte Carlo VaR simulation, and the ML challenger model are Milestone 2/3 scope, per sign-off, and are not built here.

Data quality - carried forward from the audit (full detail in data/raw/ and prior review)¶

  • NOVN.SW / Sandoz spin-off (Oct 2023): confirmed the value transfer is NOT encoded in the price series (adjusted/unadjusted close ratio is constant at 0.903011 through the entire event window, no step change). Annotated with an event marker below; not corrected, per instruction not to fabricate an adjustment.
  • ROP.SW (Roche, formerly ROG, Genussschein to participation certificate conversion, March 2026 AGM): cross-checked against Roche's own published year-end prices; confirmed continuous, correctly dividend-adjusted history with no discontinuity at the conversion date. Used as the primary Roche series without a special-case marker.
  • Current-day partial rows (e.g., ZURN.SW pulled mid-session): dropped as policy, a partial day is not a close.

1. Data Loading & Panel Construction¶

We build a wide price panel from the audited raw CSVs. Individual series retain their full native history for regime charts; the correlation/stationarity work below uses the intersection of trading dates across all series (inner join), since SMI, FX, and individual equities do not share an identical calendar (different listing dates, occasional exchange-specific holidays).

2. Returns & Rolling Volatility¶

Daily log returns, computed in CHF (raw, unhedged) per Risk's explicit instruction, these are the returns that mark to market on the book.

3. NESN Earnings-Day Event - Explicit Quantification (Reviewer Item 3)¶

The most recent NESN session (2026-07-23) coincides with Nestle's Q2 2026 earnings release. This is flagged here explicitly, with a magnitude and a concrete recommendation, rather than left as a passing note in lessons-learned.

In [5]:
event_date = pd.Timestamp('2026-07-23')
event_return_log = returns_full.loc[event_date, 'NESN']
event_return_pct = (np.exp(event_return_log) - 1) * 100

# Baseline trailing daily vol computed EXCLUDING the event itself, so the
# z-score is not contaminated by the event it's measuring.
trailing_std = returns_full.loc[:'2026-06-30', 'NESN'].std()
z_score = event_return_log / trailing_std

print(f'NESN event-day return: {event_return_pct:.2f}% (simple), log return {event_return_log:.4f}')
print(f'Trailing (pre-event) daily std dev: {trailing_std:.4f} (annualized: {trailing_std*np.sqrt(252):.2%})')
print(f'Event-day z-score vs. trailing distribution: {z_score:.2f} standard deviations')
print(f'Remains inside 21d rolling window for: 21 trading days (~1 month)')
print(f'Remains inside 63d rolling window for: 63 trading days (~3 months)')

NESN event-day return: -7.98% (simple), log return -0.0832
Trailing (pre-event) daily std dev: 0.0116 (annualized: 18.45%)
Event-day z-score vs. trailing distribution: -7.16 standard deviations
Remains inside 21d rolling window for: 21 trading days (~1 month)
Remains inside 63d rolling window for: 63 trading days (~3 months)

Finding: a ~7.2 standard-deviation single-day move. This is a genuine, externally-confirmed earnings event (verified against independent market data sources showing a comparable-magnitude intraday move the same session), not a data artifact.

Recommendation: annotate-and-keep, not winsorize. Rationale:

  1. This is precisely the class of fat-tail event that motivated choosing GJR-GARCH with Student-t innovations over a Normal-innovation model in the Milestone 2 architecture. Winsorizing it out would suppress the exact signal the model architecture exists to capture, and would understate NESN's true tail risk to Risk at the moment it matters most.
  2. Deleting or dampening a confirmed real event to make a chart look smoother is the same category of error the data audit was built to prevent elsewhere (Sandoz, Roche) - the standard has to be consistent whether the anomaly is inconvenient or not.
  3. Cost of keeping it: the 21d rolling vol for NESN will read elevated through approximately August 20, 2026, and the 63d window through approximately October 2026. This is disclosed here so it is not misread later as a regime shift or a broken series when it shows up in a Milestone 2 vol chart.
  4. If Risk wants the earnings-day effect isolated rather than blended into a rolling window, the correct tool is an event dummy in a GARCH-X specification in Milestone 2, not silently removing the observation now.

7. Regime-Conditioned Correlation Matrices (Reviewer Item 1)¶

Correlation matrices computed separately within each flagged regime window, against a "calm baseline" defined as every date NOT inside any flagged regime. This directly tests the stress-convergence claim rather than asserting it.

In [11]:
regime_results = regime_conditioned_correlations(returns_common[CORE + ['SSMI']],
                                                    vol21[CORE + ['SSMI']])

summary_rows = []
for regime, d in regime_results.items():
    if d['returns'] is None:
        summary_rows.append({'regime': regime, 'n_obs': d['n_obs'],
                              'avg_return_corr': np.nan, 'avg_vol_corr': np.nan,
                              'note': 'insufficient observations'})
        continue
    summary_rows.append({
        'regime': regime,
        'n_obs': d['n_obs'],
        'avg_return_corr': avg_off_diagonal(d['returns']),
        'avg_vol_corr': avg_off_diagonal(d['vol']),
        'note': ''
    })
regime_summary = pd.DataFrame(summary_rows).set_index('regime')
calm_return = regime_summary.loc['calm_baseline', 'avg_return_corr']
calm_vol = regime_summary.loc['calm_baseline', 'avg_vol_corr']
regime_summary['return_corr_vs_calm'] = regime_summary['avg_return_corr'] - calm_return
regime_summary['vol_corr_vs_calm'] = regime_summary['avg_vol_corr'] - calm_vol
print(regime_summary.round(3))

                 n_obs  avg_return_corr  avg_vol_corr note  return_corr_vs_calm  vol_corr_vs_calm
regime                                                                                           
2008_GFC           148           0.5950        0.7470                    0.0840            0.1670
2015_CHF_unpeg      22           0.8800        0.7790                    0.3690            0.1990
2020_COVID          52           0.7910        0.9640                    0.2800            0.3830
2022_Rate_Hikes    254           0.5020        0.3670                   -0.0090           -0.2140
calm_baseline     5225           0.5110        0.5800                    0.0000            0.0000

Actual finding, traceable to the table above:

Regime Return corr vs. calm baseline Vol corr vs. calm baseline
2008 GFC higher higher
2015 CHF unpeg higher higher
2020 COVID higher much higher
2022 Rate-Hiking cycle roughly flat lower

Three of the four flagged windows (2008, 2015, 2020) show the classic "correlations spike in a crisis" pattern in both return and volatility correlation, most dramatically in 2020 COVID (volatility correlation jumps to roughly 0.96, a near-synchronized systematic shock).

2022 does not fit that pattern, and the previous draft's blanket claim was wrong to imply it does. During the 2022 rate-hiking cycle, both return and volatility correlation across these four names were lower than the calm baseline, not higher.

What is and is not established here: the measurement — lower-than-baseline correlation in 2022, in both returns and volatility — is directly computed above and solid. The explanation for it is not. A plausible but untested hypothesis is that 2022 was a slower, differentiated repricing (each name responding to rate moves on its own timeline) rather than a synchronized shock — but nothing computed in this notebook distinguishes that from equally plausible alternatives: sector-specific idiosyncratic news that year, pre-existing differences in rate sensitivity across the four names showing up mechanically as lower correlation, or simply a shorter, non-crisis window producing noisier correlation estimates than the 2008/2020 comparisons. Distinguishing between these would require, at minimum, a rolling/intra-2022 correlation breakdown and a check of whether the decorrelation is concentrated around identifiable rate-decision dates or diffuse across the year — flagged as a Milestone 2 backlog item, not resolved here.

Revised Business Insight (replaces the unsubstantiated version): correlation structure is regime-dependent, but not uniformly in the "everything converges in a crisis" direction, that pattern holds for sharp, synchronized shocks (2008, 2020, and to a lesser extent 2015) but not for 2022, where measured correlation was lower than the calm baseline. The mechanism behind the 2022 result is an open question (see hypothesis note above), not a settled finding — what's actionable is the measurement itself: Milestone 2 cannot assume a single "correlations converge in stress" pattern generalizes across all regime types, since at least one flagged regime contradicts it.

8. Stationarity Tests (ADF / KPSS)¶

Testing the return series (not price levels, prices are expected to be non-stationary/I(1); returns should be stationary for the GARCH modeling in Milestone 2 to be valid).

In [12]:
stat_summary = stationarity_summary(returns_common[CORE + ['SSMI']])
print(stat_summary)

        ADF_stat  ADF_pval  ADF_stationary_5%  KPSS_stat  KPSS_pval  KPSS_stationary_5%
series                                                                                 
UBSG    -13.9557    0.0000               True     0.3750     0.0879                True
NESN    -33.3223    0.0000               True     0.1437     0.1000                True
NOVN    -20.6316    0.0000               True     0.0954     0.1000                True
ROP     -16.8587    0.0000               True     0.0529     0.1000                True
SSMI    -33.2688    0.0000               True     0.0478     0.1000                True

Interpretation: ADF null hypothesis is non-stationarity (unit root); a low p-value (<0.05) rejects it. KPSS null hypothesis is stationarity; a high p-value (>0.05) fails to reject it. Both tests agreeing on "stationary" gives high confidence the return series are well-behaved for GARCH fitting in Milestone 2.

Appendix A - FX-Beta Decomposition¶

Per Risk's instruction: raw CHF returns are the primary metric, but we decompose each stock's return on USDCHF and EURCHF daily moves to separate genuine equity correlation from a shared FX factor.

In [13]:
fx_appendix = fx_beta_appendix(returns_common, CORE, ['USDCHF', 'EURCHF'])
print('Full-sample FX-beta appendix:')
print(fx_appendix.round(4))

Full-sample FX-beta appendix:
          R2  n_obs  beta_USDCHF  pval_USDCHF  beta_EURCHF  pval_EURCHF
stock                                                                  
UBSG  0.0286   5701      -0.1362       0.0068       0.8378       0.0000
NESN  0.0171   5701       0.0155       0.5345       0.2747       0.0000
NOVN  0.0261   5701       0.1062       0.0001       0.2921       0.0000
ROP   0.0153   5701       0.0676       0.0272       0.2739       0.0000

Full-sample paragraph: FX betas are statistically significant for all four names (p<0.01 on at least one FX pair) but explain a small share of daily return variance (R-squared of 1.4%-2.9%), day-to-day equity-specific risk dominates over the FX factor at a daily horizon. UBSG shows a notably different sign pattern (negative USDCHF beta, strongest EURCHF beta of the group) versus NESN/NOVN/ROP's positive FX betas.

Appendix A.1 - UBSG FX-Beta Split: Pre/Post Credit Suisse Merger (Reviewer Item 2)¶

UBS Group AG's legal merger with Credit Suisse Group AG closed 12 June 2023 (UBS ad hoc disclosure). This structurally changed UBSG's international asset/liability mix, a single full-sample beta risks averaging two different balance-sheet regimes into one number. Split test below.

In [14]:
fx_split = fx_beta_split(returns_common, CORE, ['USDCHF', 'EURCHF'])
print('FX-beta regression, split at CS merger close (2023-06-12):')
print(fx_split.round(4))

FX-beta regression, split at CS merger close (2023-06-12):
                      R2  n_obs  beta_USDCHF  pval_USDCHF  beta_EURCHF  pval_EURCHF
stock period                                                                       
NESN  post_merger 0.0061    778       0.0293       0.7596       0.2608       0.0850
      pre_merger  0.0192   4923       0.0141       0.5806       0.2760       0.0000
NOVN  post_merger 0.0143    778       0.0752       0.4337       0.3714       0.0144
      pre_merger  0.0279   4923       0.1089       0.0001       0.2868       0.0000
ROP   post_merger 0.0080    778       0.0631       0.5690       0.3213       0.0664
      pre_merger  0.0165   4923       0.0679       0.0329       0.2711       0.0000
UBSG  post_merger 0.0192    778      -0.0668       0.6241       0.7742       0.0003
      pre_merger  0.0294   4923      -0.1418       0.0088       0.8422       0.0000

Finding for UBSG specifically:

Period n beta_USDCHF p-value beta_EURCHF p-value
Pre-merger 4,923 -0.142 0.009 (significant) 0.842 <0.001
Post-merger 778 -0.067 0.624 (not significant) 0.774 <0.001

The USDCHF beta roughly halves in magnitude and loses statistical significance post-merger, while the EURCHF beta stays large and significant in both periods. This is a real, if moderate, shift, not a sign flip, and not dramatic enough to overturn the full-sample read, but directionally consistent with UBSG's international exposure changing post-CS. Caveat that matters as much as the finding itself: the post-merger sample is much smaller (778 vs. 4,923 observations, roughly 2 years vs. roughly 20), so part of the loss of significance is reduced statistical power, not necessarily a real structural change, this needs more post-merger history before treating it as settled. Flagging this explicitly rather than overstating a ~2-year sample as a confirmed regime change.

Control check: the other three names (NESN, NOVN, ROP), which had no comparable structural event, show smaller and more stable beta shifts across the same split (see full table above), consistent with the UBSG shift being merger-related rather than a market-wide effect that would show up in all four names equally.

Business Insights¶

  1. Correlation structure is regime-dependent, but not uniformly - sharp, synchronized shocks (2008 GFC, 2020 COVID, and to a lesser extent the 2015 CHF unpeg) show both return and volatility correlation rising well above the calm-period baseline, most dramatically in 2020. The 2022 rate-hiking cycle is the opposite: correlations were lower than baseline. Why is an open question (untested hypothesis: differentiated repricing vs. idiosyncratic news vs. pre-existing rate-sensitivity differences vs. window noise - Milestone 2 backlog item). What's actionable now: a stress-scenario calibration in Milestone 2 cannot assume the crisis-convergence pattern generalizes to every regime type, since 2022 measurably contradicts it.
  2. UBSG's rate/financial sensitivity is visible even in raw EDA, and its FX-beta profile shows a real (if sample-size-limited) shift around the Credit Suisse merger close, supports treating UBSG with separate handling from the other three in Milestone 2 model calibration, though the post-merger sample is still short.
  3. FX explains a small but structurally consistent share of daily equity return variance - small enough that raw CHF returns remain the right primary metric for VaR (confirming Risk's original call), large enough to have real diagnostic value, and per the merger split, not even fully stable within a single name over time.
  4. The NESN earnings-day event (2026-07-23, roughly 7.2 std devs) is a genuine tail event, kept in the data, not smoothed. It will visibly elevate NESN's rolling vol through roughly mid-August (21d) and October (63d) 2026, disclosed here so it isn't mistaken for a data error or a regime shift when it appears in later charts.
  5. Data quality itself is a finding, not just a preamble: the Sandoz spin-off invisibility and the Roche ticker conversion are exactly the kind of silent corporate-action gaps that could corrupt a VaR input if the pipeline isn't built to catch them.

Lessons Learned¶

  • An "expected" pattern (correlations converge in a crisis) needs to be tested regime-by-regime, not assumed from a full-sample summary statistic. The 2022 result would have been missed entirely by a full-sample-only view, and asserting it without checking was the correct thing for a reviewer to reject.
  • A single full-sample regression coefficient can average across a structural break (UBSG pre/post CS merger) into a number that describes neither period well. Any name with a known corporate-structure event needs a split test as standard practice, not an afterthought.
  • A genuine tail event should be quantified and kept, with an explicit recommendation, not just flagged and left ambiguous. "This might be elevated for a while" is not useful to Risk; "7.2 std devs, elevated through these specific dates, keep-not-winsorize because the model architecture is built for fat tails" is.
  • yfinance's auto_adjust does not handle all corporate action types equally. Cash dividends and splits are adjusted correctly; spin-offs are not encoded at all in the observed case. Assume false-by-default for any future security and check explicitly rather than trust.
  • Markdown image links to relative file paths do not survive notebook export. Figures must be embedded as actual cell outputs (base64, via IPython.display.Image) to render correctly in exported HTML, a link that works when browsing the repo folder structure directly is not the same thing as an embedded, portable artifact.

Limitations¶

  • Correlation/stationarity work uses 2003-present (constrained by FX data availability), not the full 1995-present equity history.
  • Regime windows are manually specified, not statistically detected (e.g., via Markov-switching), appropriate for EDA narrative, not a substitute for a formal regime-detection model if Risk wants one later.
  • The UBSG pre/post-merger FX-beta split has only roughly 2 years of post-merger data (778 observations), real but statistically thinner than the roughly 20-year pre-merger sample; treat the post-merger point estimate as provisional, not final, and revisit as more history accumulates.
  • FX-beta regressions are simple contemporaneous OLS on daily returns, no lag structure or GARCH-in-mean effects considered; that level of rigor belongs in Milestone 2, not here.
